steps.say: Prolapse staging used to be a shrug and a finger estimate until the POP-Q grid made it a measurement. The POP-Q system takes the hymenal ring as its zero reference plane and scores how far each vaginal compartment sits above or below it in centimetres. Anterior, apical, and posterior descent are each graded, so two surgeons in different cities describe the same bulge identically.
steps.tx: Stage every prolapse with the **POP-Q system** (measured prolapse grid, Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification), which sets the **hymenal ring** (vaginal opening rim) as the **zero reference** (measurement datum) plane. Anterior, apical, and posterior compartment descent are each graded above or below the hymen in centimetres, so the grid replaces vague impressions with reproducible stages that guide repair choice and audit.

vis.alt: Diagram of POP-Q points grid and prolapse stages on pelvic examination.
vis.caption: POP-Q points and stages: the hymen is the zero plane for all compartments. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: When the vaginal apex itself collapses, stitching the front wall alone will fail again within years. Abdominal or robotic sacrocolpopexy suspends the apex with a lightweight polypropylene mesh bridge anchored to the anterior longitudinal ligament of the sacrum at S1. This apical suspension is the gold standard repair for apical prolapse, with the lowest repeat surgery rate of any operation.
steps.tx: Repair **apical prolapse** (vault or uterine descent) with abdominal or robotic **sacrocolpopexy** (mesh vault suspension), anchoring lightweight polypropylene mesh to the **longitudinal sacral ligament** (anterior spinal ligament) at S1 (first sacral bone). The mesh bridge holds the apex high permanently, making sacrocolpopexy the **gold standard repair** (lowest failure rate) for apical defects, while isolated anterior repairs sag again without apical support.

vis.alt: Surgical illustration of anterior colporrhaphy repairing the front vaginal wall.
vis.caption: Anterior wall repair: lasting only when the apex is suspended as well. Credit: Wikipedia Medical.

steps.say: A woman leaking urine continuously after childbirth or pelvic surgery has a fistula until proven otherwise. In developing countries the vesicovaginal fistula follows prolonged obstructed labor, where the trapped head strangles bladder blood supply into ischemic necrosis. In developed nations 80 to 90 percent follow iatrogenic injury, mostly abdominal hysterectomy nicking the bladder, so the cause map flips with the setting.
steps.tx: Trace every **vesicovaginal fistula** (**VVF**, bladder to vagina hole) to its setting: prolonged **obstructed labor** (trapped head causing ischemic necrosis) dominates developing countries, while **80% to 90%** (eight to nine in ten) follow **hysterectomy** (womb removal surgery, iatrogenic gynecologic injury) in developed nations. The history already halves the workup: labour fistulae sit low and wide, while surgical fistulae follow the hysterectomy plane near the vault.

steps.say: Two holes can both leak into the vagina, and the double dye test tells them apart at the bedside. The patient swallows phenazopyridine, which turns kidney urine bright orange, while methylene blue is washed into the bladder through a catheter. A blue stained tampon proves a vesicovaginal hole, while an orange tampon convicts the ureter, all without a single scan.
steps.tx: Separate bladder from ureter leaks with the **double dye test** (two colour bedside test): oral **phenazopyridine** (kidney dye turning urine orange) plus intravesical **methylene blue** (bladder dye) instillation, then inspect a vaginal tampon. Blue staining confirms **VVF** (bladder hole leak), while orange staining confirms **ureterovaginal fistula** (ureter hole leak), triaging the patient to vaginal versus abdominal repair before imaging.

steps.say: Not every fistula needs the abdomen opened. The Latzko partial colpocleisis closes supratrigonal post hysterectomy fistulae entirely through the vagina, denuding and sewing the vaginal wall over the hole without touching the ureteral openings or the bladder neck. Cure rates are reported above 95 percent for these high vault holes, with a one night stay and a dry patient.
steps.tx: Close post-hysterectomy vault holes vaginally with **Latzko colpocleisis** (partial vaginal closure, **Latzko** denudation technique) for **supratrigonal fistula** (hole above the bladder triangle): denude vaginal epithelium around the tract and sew it buried, sparing ureteral orifices and bladder neck. Cure exceeds **95%** (ninety five in a hundred) for supratrigonal defects, so reserve abdominal surgery for low, large, or radiation damaged holes.

steps.say: Big or awkward fistulae need the bladder opened and rebuilt. The O'Conor technique splits the bladder vertically from dome down to the fistula, freeing wide flaps around the tract, then closes the bladder and vagina in separate layers. A tongue of omentum is tucked between the two suture lines as a vascularised interposition graft, so the holes can never kiss and reopen.
steps.tx: Rebuild complex defects with the **O'Conor technique** (bladder splitting repair): **bisection of bladder** (vertical dome to fistula split) mobilises flaps around the tract for layered bladder and vaginal closure, separated by an **omental flap** (fatty apron tongue) as a vascularized **interposition graft** (living tissue barrier). The graft brings blood and blocks reapposition, making O'Conor the workhorse for large, high, or previously failed fistulae.

rows: Bisection of bladder to the tract

steps.say: Radiation and repeat failures starve tissue of blood, and sewing dead edges together only fails again. The Martius flap harvests a pad of labial fat with its own vessels and tunnels it into the repair as a vascularized interposition graft. This living filler rescues complex, recurrent, and post radiation vesicovaginal and urethrovaginal fistulae that plain closure cannot heal.
steps.tx: Salvage ischaemic repairs with the **Martius flap** (labial fat pad graft): tunnelled fibrofatty tissue brings its own blood as an **interposition graft** (vascular filler) for complex, recurrent, or **radiation fistula** (post radiotherapy holes) of vesicovaginal and urethrovaginal type. Well fed edges heal where starved edges split, so any repair in irradiated or multiply operated tissue earns a flap, never bare sutures.

rows: Martius flap, labial fat with vessels

steps.say: Haste is punished in radiation fistulae above all. Tissues keep dying for months after the last session, so stitching early means stitching dying edges that melt apart. Every radiation induced hole waits at least six to twelve months after radiation ends, and every repair carries a vascularized flap, because only imported blood can heal a burnt field.
steps.tx: Delay surgery for **radiation-induced VVF** (post radiotherapy holes) to at least **6 to 12 months** (six to twelve months) after radiation cessation: a **delayed repair** (waiting out tissue death) lets necrosis declare itself before stitches go in. Combine delay with mandatory vascularized flap transfer, because irradiated beds heal only with imported blood. Early bare repair of a radiation fistula fails twice: once from timing, once from starvation.
